question: Does the DeMix/OpenCompass evaluation contract change between the public OpenCompass 0.5.1 publication line and 0.5.2 because of OpenCompass source changes, dependency-resolution changes, or both?

observed_source_delta.implication: Because setup.py derives install_requires from requirements/runtime.txt with version specifiers preserved, the pandas/pyext delta is part of the install contract, not merely a development-file difference.
observed_source_delta.generation_path: 0.5.2 adds optional dump_res_length instrumentation to GenInferencer and optional res_length/input_length fields to GenInferencerOutputHandler. The option defaults false, so this observed change alone is not evidence that default benchmark predictions or scores change.

track_A_code_isolation.rule: Use one shared, explicit dependency lock that satisfies both source trees, including pandas<2.0.0 and identical Python/Torch/Transformers/datasets/mmengine/tokenizer/runtime packages. Use the same model bytes, dataset bytes/configs, seeds, backend, batch size, prompt hashes, and evaluator settings.

track_B_package_native.rule: Install each public package/source line according to its own declared runtime constraints in separately locked fresh environments, then freeze the fully resolved lock before evaluation. Do not call any difference a source-code effect because 0.5.2 permits dependency states, including pandas>=2, that 0.5.1 forbids.

interpretation.A_diff_B_diff: source and/or shared dependency runtime effects exist; localize with file/path ablations
interpretation.A_same_B_diff: package dependency-resolution sensitivity dominates observed version difference
interpretation.A_diff_B_same: unlikely but possible cancellation under native environments; investigate exact resolved locks
interpretation.A_same_B_same: public 0.5.1->0.5.2 version change is behaviorally neutral for this exact fixture within measured precision

scope_guards: This does not prove which OpenCompass environment DeMix authors actually used.
The observed optional result-length instrumentation is not evidence of score change under default settings.
A package-native comparison is not a code-only comparison unless dependency locks are identical.
Any conclusions apply only to the exact nine-benchmark fixture, model/backend/data/config versions, seeds and dependency locks tested.
exact_next_action: Build Track A first with a common lock satisfying both anchors; then run Track B with independently resolved public package constraints. Persist locks and all raw/hash/schema artifacts before interpreting score deltas.
